newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian coconut oil softens, copra up.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian coconut oil softens, copra up.

text.p: Indonesian coconut oil prices suffered extended losses amid poor market sentiment on Thursday, but copra was higher on rising demand, traders said.

"Coconut oil prices continue to fall because oil is abundant in the market. On the other hand, copra prices are up because industrial demand such as from cookie factories is quite high," said one trader in Jakarta.
Traders said consumer demand for copra was also high from buyers who would later sell it in local markets. Coconut oil was quoted at 1,790 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, down from 1,810-20 a week ago.
Copra was higher at 800 rupiah/kg from 730 a week ago.
Traders said the trend in the local coconut oil market stayed bearish as demand continued to be poor, adding that copra supply was ample in Indonesia.

Some traders attributed the fall to the rising demand for palm olein, a substitute for coconut oil, whose prices were usually cheaper. Palm olein was quoted at 1,410-15 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, compared with 1,410 rupiah at Wednesday's close, on keen buying interest ahead of the Eid al-Adha celebration on Friday.
Manila vegetable oil traders said on Monday coconut oil prices are expected to slide this week due to rising supplies.
Indonesia is the world's second largest coconut producer after the Philippines and local traders often look to Manila for price direction.
Some Indonesian traders said they expected the prices to improve next week as stock in Rotterdam had started to decline.
Data released on Monday showed that coconut oil stocks in Rotterdam were 21,765 tonnes against 23,704 tonnes the week before.
